Title: Lim Guan Eng cites fresh LCS delays in renewing scrutiny of Zahid’s ‘please implement’ note
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — DAP’s Lim Guan Eng today cited fresh delays to Malaysia’s Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project in renewing scrutiny of Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s role in the procurement when he was defence minister.
In a statement, the Bagan MP referred to the latest findings in the 2026 Auditor-General’s Report, which found that the RM11.22 billion project was 7.55 per cent behind schedule as of June 25.
Lim also referred to a July 8, 2010 letter from Boustead Naval Shipyard (BNS) to Ahmad Zahid, then defence minister, seeking a letter of intent from the government for the LCS project.
A handwritten note attributed to Ahmad Zahid on the letter read: “SUB [Division Secretary] Procurement, please implement.”
“The words ‘please implement’ continue to haunt Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over the RM11.22 billion purchase of five LCS,” Lim said.
The letter was among documents contained in a report by the Special Investigation Committee on Governance, Procurement and Finance that was declassified in 2022.
According to the latest Auditor-General’s Report, progress on the LCS project was 7.55 per cent behind schedule as of June 25, with delays ranging from 30 to 108 days.
The report said the delay could affect the physical handover of LCS 1, which had initially been scheduled for August 26 and now has a revised target date of December 26.
It also said the ship could be handed over without full operational capability because training and weapons systems had yet to be completed.
Full operational readiness for the programme depends on a supplementary contract that is expected to be completed in December 2035, beyond the April 25, 2030 expiry of the main contract.
The Auditor-General also said delays to LCS 1 could affect the delivery schedule for the remaining four vessels.
Lim said the longer timeline raised questions over whether some of the technology used in the ships could become outdated before the programme achieved full operational readiness.
“Apart from the loss of billions of ringgit, a 24-year delay in the delivery of the LCS by 2035 for an order placed in 2011 would inevitably raise questions over whether the technology used in the ships would have become obsolete and outdated,” he said.
Lim’s calculation of 24 years spans the period from the project’s procurement in 2011 to the 2035 target for full operational readiness, rather than representing a 24-year delay against the original ship-delivery schedule.
The LCS programme was originally for six vessels under a RM9.128 billion contract, with the first ship due in 2019 and the remaining vessels to be delivered by 2023.
The project was later restructured, reducing the order to five ships while increasing the contract value to about RM11.22 billion.
The project drew widespread attention in 2022 after the Public Accounts Committee disclosed that RM6.083 billion had been paid as of October 2020 despite none of the six ships having been delivered.
BNS was subsequently renamed Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd, or Lunas, with the government stepping in through a Ministry of Finance-owned vehicle as part of efforts to complete the project.
By the end of 2025, expenditure on the project had risen to about RM8.3 billion, while construction of the first vessel had moved into shipyard-level sea trials.

Title: After Irene Sofiya’s death, Suhakam calls for nationwide overhaul of school safeguarding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Suhakam’s Children’s Commissioners have called for nationwide reforms to school safeguarding following the death of 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, including tighter student check-out procedures, missing-student protocols and audits of safety gaps on school grounds.
In a statement today, the commissioners said schools needed to move beyond conventional security measures towards a “proactive, child-centred safeguarding culture”, particularly for activities held outside normal school hours.
“Every child has an inherent right to an education in a safe, secure, and protective environment,” they said.
Among the measures proposed were formal procedures to account for students during extra classes, co-curricular activities and sports training, as well as clear escalation protocols setting out when parents, school administrators and police should be alerted if a student goes missing.
They also called for targeted risk assessments of after-school activities, when staffing may be lower and pupils may move through isolated or poorly supervised parts of school grounds, alongside nationwide safeguarding audits examining student movement, reporting mechanisms and physical blind spots.
The recommendations come as police continue investigating Irene’s death at a school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, on Saturday.
The commissioners stressed that the criminal investigation and a broader Education Ministry safeguarding review were separate but complementary processes.
While police were responsible for establishing the facts and determining any criminal culpability, the ministry should examine supervision, risk management, administrative procedures and physical safety measures for possible systemic gaps, they said.
“Raising these broader systemic questions is essential for preventive risk management and does not imply or constitute a finding of institutional failure in this specific case,” they said.
The commissioners also urged the public, media and social media users not to speculate about the circumstances of Irene’s death, including unverified claims of bullying, while investigations were continuing.
They called for restraint over premature accusations and a “trial by media”, saying the privacy, dignity and presumption of innocence of any children involved as witnesses, affected pupils or individuals under investigation must be protected.
“Protecting the legal rights and confidentiality of children under investigation in no way diminishes the severity of the loss, nor does it preclude accountability in accordance with the law,” they said.
Irene, a Form Four student, was found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall at about 5.50pm on Saturday.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said she had suffered multiple injuries to her head and body and was pronounced dead at the scene.
A 16-year-old boy was detained in Yong Peng at about 7pm that day and remanded for six days until October 9 to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Police have said the motive and circumstances surrounding the case remain under investigation.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has ordered a comprehensive review of school management and security following Irene’s death.
She said yesterday that while the school was equipped with CCTV cameras, none had been installed at the location where the incident occurred.
The ministry was also investigating the school’s security company to determine whether there had been any breach of standard operating procedures, she said.
Beyond physical security, the Children’s Commissioners called for immediate trauma-informed psychosocial support for affected pupils and teachers, saying child witnesses should not be subjected to unnecessary repeated questioning.
They also said schools should ensure reporting channels were confidential, accessible and trusted by pupils so children knew where to seek help if they felt unsafe or noticed warning signs among their peers.
“Children should be recognised as active partners in their own safety,” the commissioners said.
They said Irene’s death should serve as a catalyst for sustained reforms to child protection across Malaysian schools, with clearer accountability and stronger safeguarding frameworks.
“This heartbreaking incident must serve as a catalyst for meaningful, sustained, and nationwide institutional reform,” they said.

Title: SUPP mourns passing of party loyalist, ‘father of hawkers’ Song Swee Guan
Article:
MIRI, Oct 6 — The Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) has paid tribute to veteran member and former leader Datuk Song Swee Guan, who passed away Sunday at the age of 84.
SUPP secretary-general Datuk Sebastian Ting said the party was deeply saddened by the passing of Kuching South’s first mayor, and extended his condolences on behalf of the leadership and all members.
“Song devoted a significant part of his life to public service and to serving the people of Sarawak, in particular Kuching.
“Throughout his long career, he served in many important capacities, including as state assemblyman for Padungan, Member of Parliament for Bandar Kuching, and Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly,” he said in a statement.
“He will always occupy a special place in the history of Kuching.”
Ting said as Kuching South’s founding mayor in August 1988, Song helped lay the foundations for the development and administration of Kuching South, serving until 1996.
“He was was known as the ‘father of hawkers’ during his time as mayor. He was also among the pioneers in greening the city, and his policies on education, urban poverty eradication, job creation, vocational training and infrastructure development have been described as the cornerstone of today’s Kuching South,” he added.
Song was Padungan assemblyman for four terms from 1983 to 2001, and Bandar Kuching MP from 1995 to 2003.
In November 1996, he was appointed State Legislative Assembly Speaker, a post he held until 2000.
Ting said that within SUPP, Song was a dedicated party member and leader who served the party and the people for many years.
“His association with the Padungan area, in particular, formed an important chapter in SUPP’s history of service in Kuching.
“While we mourn his passing, we also remember with gratitude his years of dedication, sacrifice and contribution to SUPP, to Kuching, and to Sarawak,” he said.
Ting last night accompanied SUPP president Deputy Premier Datuk Dr Sim Kui Hian and other party leaders in paying their last respects to Song. — The Borneo Post

Title: Higher education minister: 1.16 million PTPTN borrowers have RM10.7b in outstanding repayments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Some 1.16 million National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers had RM10.7 billion in outstanding loan repayments as of August 31, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the figure represented the latest total of outstanding repayments owed to PTPTN.
“The total outstanding loan repayments of the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) as of August 31, 2026 was RM10.7 billion involving 1.16 million borrowers,” he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Zambry said various initiatives had been and would continue to be undertaken to ensure the long-term sustainability of PTPTN’s funding model.
These included strengthening loan management by improving loan terms and conditions to ensure funding was more targeted towards those in need, based on PTPTN’s capacity.
He said the government would also improve the effectiveness and efficiency of repayment collection through enforcement measures and strategic cooperation with government agencies and corporations.
However, Zambry said the government remained mindful of borrowers who were genuinely facing difficulties in making repayments.
He said PTPTN remained open to such borrowers coming forward for discussions on restructuring their repayments according to their ability, or deferring repayments subject to the flexibility allowed by the corporation.
In March last year, Zambry told the Dewan Negara that outstanding PTPTN repayments stood at RM11.06 billion involving 1.2 million borrowers as of December 31, 2024.
He said at the time that the amount had been declining following repayment enforcement measures reintroduced in October 2024.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu), who asked the higher education minister for the latest amount in outstanding PTPTN repayments and the measures being taken to increase loan repayments.

Title: New Bar Course expected in 2028, or 2029 at latest, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia’s New Bar Course (NBC) is expected to be implemented in 2028, or by 2029 at the latest, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said.
Azalina said the timeline took into account the preparations required and policies that still needed to be formulated by the Legal Profession Qualifying Board before the course could be rolled out.
She said the board established the New Bar Course Task Force on April 27, 2026, to conduct a study and develop an operational framework for the NBC.
“The main objective of the NBC study is to develop an operational framework for the implementation of the NBC and ensure that planning to realise the NBC runs smoothly,” she said in a written parliamentary reply.
Azalina said the board and the task force were taking the necessary steps towards implementation, including preparing course content modules for the Conversion Course (CC) and Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC) programmes, as well as a question bank.
Other preparations include procuring a Learning Management System and Computer-Based Assessment system for the NBC, drafting academic regulations for the CC and LPPC programmes, and strengthening the board’s organisational structure and workforce to operate the programmes.
The board is also planning capacity-building for paper setters, examiners and assessors, while criteria are being drawn up for course providers seeking to conduct the LPPC.
The New Bar Course is intended to form part of reforms to Malaysia’s system for qualifying law graduates for legal practice, with the proposed framework covering conversion training and postgraduate professional preparation.
The initiative is being developed under the Legal Profession Qualifying Board, which oversees professional qualification requirements for admission to legal practice in Malaysia.
Azalina was responding to a question from Kesavan Subramaniam (PH-Sungai Siput), who asked for the latest status of the Legal Profession Qualifying Board’s implementation of the NBC and when the course was expected to begin.

Title: Police seek man over mosque vandalism in Tumpat
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 6 — Police are identifying a man believed to be linked to the vandalism of the Al-Aziz Al-Hadi Mosque in Kota SPP Warisan, Tumpat, yesterday.
Tumpat police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said CCTV footage from the mosque showed a man believed to be connected to the incident, which occurred at 6.35am.
He said police received a report from a member of the public, while initial checks found that the mosque’s glass door had been smashed and a foul-smelling, greenish-brown liquid poured onto the carpet in the prayer hall.
“The case is being investigated under Sections 295 and 427 of the Penal Code,” he said in a statement last night.
Mohd Khairi said police were also investigating the motive and assessing the extent of the damage or losses incurred.
He urged the public not to speculate, make accusations or spread unverified information, and advised anyone with information to contact the Tumpat District Police Headquarters operations room at 09-725 6226. — Bernama

Title: Defence minister: Strengthening cooperation, system resilience among focuses in tackling cyber threats in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Cyber threats have the potential to destroy national critical infrastructure and escalate into a national crisis.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said new forms of cyberattacks could paralyse essential systems and daily services.
He said critical infrastructure at risk includes airports, ports, banking systems, healthcare facilities and internet networks.
“Jammed communications can create uncertainty and panic. Interruptions to transportation can halt the movement of people and goods.
“Disruptions in energy supplies can paralyse almost every sector of our economy. When these systems fail, what begins as an invisible attack can quickly escalate into a national crisis,” he said.
He outlined four key considerations to strengthen cyber resilience, namely maintaining human accountability, ensuring system resilience, investing in human capital and strengthening cooperation.
Mohamed Khaled said resilience in defence systems involves preventing cyberattacks and the ability to withstand disruptions, recover quickly, and continue operations.
He said this in his speech at the opening of the Siber Siaga 2026 programme held in conjunction with the Cyber Digital Services, Defence and Security Asia (CyberDSA) 2026 exhibition at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here yesterday.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) Headquarters said in a statement that the Siber Siaga programme is MAF’s main strategic initiative to build comprehensive national cyber resilience.
The statement said the initiative led by the Cyber and Electromagnetic Command (PSEP) positions MAF as a pioneer in integrating multi-stakeholder strategic cooperation.
Efforts to construct the cyber resilience ecosystem combine collaboration between MAF, the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA), CyberSecurity Malaysia, and higher learning institutions such as the National Defence University of Malaysia (UPNM).
With the theme “Hyperwar: Man, Machine, Decision”, Siber Siaga focuses on the security forces’ approach to new-generation warfare involving artificial intelligence, automation and autonomous systems. — Bernama

Title: Kulim boy, 13, seriously injured in school incident amid reported academic stress
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A 13-year-old boy was seriously injured in an incident at a secondary school in Kulim, Kedah, with police saying he had been experiencing stress over his studies and upcoming examinations.
Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 3.40pm on Sunday during a school break.
Police received a report from a 48-year-old male teacher after the student was found injured near a staircase at the school.
“The complainant went to the location and found the victim still conscious and able to speak before he was taken to Kulim Hospital for treatment,” Syamsul said in a statement today.
He said police later spoke to the boy, who told investigators that he had been under pressure over his academic performance.
Syamsul said the boy was also worried about examinations scheduled for next week and whether he would be able to meet his parents’ expectations.
“According to the victim, examinations will be held next week and he was worried that he would not be able to meet his parents’ expectations,” he said.

Title: Malaysia’s border control agency seizes RM11.8m cocoa consignment from Uganda at Pasir Gudang Port
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 6 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has seized cocoa beans worth RM11.8 million, which were attempted to be smuggled into the country in a container from Uganda at Pasir Gudang Port here on October 3.
In a statement, AKPS said the seizure of 637,000 kilogrammes of cocoa beans was made following an inspection by enforcement officers at 3.50 pm.
“The goods were found to have been brought into the country with incomplete and suspicious documents, resulting in the entire consignment being detained for further investigation,” it said.
AKPS stressed that any attempt to declare conflicting data at the country’s entry points constitutes an offence under Section 13 of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 [Act 728].
According to the agency, upon conviction, the parties involved may be fined up to RM50,000 or imprisoned for a term not exceeding two years, or both, while for a second or subsequent offence, they may be fined up to RM75,000 or imprisoned for a term not exceeding five years, or both.
AKPS said it viewed such activities seriously and would continue to carry out enforcement at the country’s entry points. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry: Myanmar nationals undergo rigorous screening before repatriation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — All Myanmar nationals involved in the first phase of the repatriation programme in Lumut, Perak, on September 29 underwent rigorous screening and verification before being repatriated voluntarily, safely, and with dignity to their home country.
The Home Ministry (KDN) said the process covered citizenship verification, documentation, health screening and identity checks.
According to the ministry, the Myanmar government verified the list of individuals and submitted it to Malaysia through a diplomatic note dated August 13, followed by detailed coordination on security, logistics, and reception arrangements in Myanmar.
“For the first phase, final processing was carried out at the Manjung District Stadium before the individuals were taken to the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) Base in Lumut for repatriation.
“The government ensures that the repatriation process is carried out safely, orderly, responsibly and with dignity, in accordance with the procedures agreed upon by both countries,” the ministry said in a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document on the programme.
The ministry said the programme is part of the government’s approach to addressing irregular migration and undocumented migrants through enforcement, detention management and orderly, safe and responsible repatriation.
The measure also helps reduce unnecessary detention periods, thereby easing pressure on the capacity and operating costs of Immigration Detention Depots (DTI).
“As of August 31, there were 11,804 Myanmar nationals detained at Immigration Detention Depots and Baitul Mahabbah facilities nationwide,” it said.
The ministry said the high number of detainees and prolonged detention periods had placed pressure on depot capacity and resulted in significant government expenditure.
The repatriation programme was therefore established as a bilateral initiative between Malaysia and Myanmar to facilitate the phased return of Myanmar nationals detained in Malaysia.
It said the Myanmar government had committed to accepting the return of 5,000 of its citizens throughout 2026.
Under the programme, KDN acts as the coordinating ministry, while the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) serves as the main operational agency.
The operation also involves the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, National Security Council, Ministry of Defence, Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) and other relevant security agencies.
The first phase on September 29 saw 1,476 Myanmar nationals repatriated aboard three Myanmar Navy vessels, including a hospital ship.
The operation involved detainees from 14 Immigration Detention Depots nationwide, with the largest numbers coming from the Belantik Depot in Kedah and Tanah Merah Depot in Kelantan.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil previously said an agreement had been reached for the voluntary repatriation of 3,524 Myanmar detainees under the programme’s second phase. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu tells Perikatan to stop ‘playing victim’ as coalition feud deepens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia has accused Perikatan Nasional (PN) of trying to “play the victim” in the coalition’s deepening internal crisis, saying its leadership should answer allegations against it with facts and documents rather than portray itself as being unfairly targeted.
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said PN should not push narratives unsupported by evidence or suggest that others were acting cowardly or oppressing the coalition without justification.
“PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan needs to answer whether it is true that Bersatu lodged complaints over the management of the coalition,” he said in a statement last night.
“There is no need to spin the issue. Just rebut, one by one, the complaints raised by Bersatu, as conveyed by the Registrar of Societies to Takiyuddin, with evidence.”
Tun Faisal said that if PAS, which administers PN, had not breached the coalition’s constitution, its leaders should produce the relevant meeting minutes, correspondence and other documents.
“If PAS, as the administrator of PN, did not commit any breach of the PN constitution, then simply provide the explanations, meeting minutes, correspondence and relevant documents to rebut each allegation,” he said.
“If he has them, answer the RoS without making so many excuses. That would be courageous.”
The remarks were aimed at Takiyuddin, who had described Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin as cowardly for allegedly failing to raise the party’s grievances clearly and officially with PN.
Takiyuddin, who is also PAS secretary-general, had likened the move to “throwing a stone and hiding the hand”, while saying PN had sought a judicial review of action taken against the coalition by the Registrar of Societies.
Tun Faisal rejected the criticism and turned the accusation back on PN’s leadership, saying cowardice was a more fitting description for administrators who, in his view, had failed to convene meetings and face disputes with component parties openly.
“Do not talk about courage if chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and PN’s administrators do not dare face their own component party. This is the real cowardice,” he said.
He also accused PAS of repeatedly breaching PN’s constitution, disregarding decisions of the coalition’s supreme council and denying Bersatu its rights as a member.
The latest exchange comes amid a wider dispute that has drawn intervention from the Registrar of Societies.
On September 22, the RoS issued PN with a notice seeking an explanation over complaints reportedly lodged by Bersatu. The following day, the regulator suspended all of PN’s activities under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966.
The action has since become the subject of a court challenge, with PN seeking judicial review of the RoS notices.
The row has also exposed increasingly bitter tensions between PAS and Bersatu, the two main parties in PN, with both sides trading accusations over how the coalition has been managed and whether decisions taken by its leadership complied with its own constitution.

Title: Economy Ministry gets 9,955 project proposals worth RM944b for 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Economy Ministry has received 9,955 new and extension project proposals totalling RM944 billion for 2027.
The ministry said RM80.4 billion was required as the 2027 development expenditure ceiling for consideration under the development planning process.
“Under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030, ministries and agencies may submit proposals for development programmes and projects for consideration by the Economy Ministry through the rolling plan process,” it said in a written reply published on the Malaysian parliament website yesterday.
The ministry was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Anak Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) on the mechanism to ensure every development project announcement includes clear allocations, implementation timelines, targets and responsible agencies.
It said engagement sessions with ministries, state governments and relevant agencies were also held to prioritise projects based on needs, implementation capacity and stipulated timelines.
“This is to ensure approved projects are implemented in an orderly manner, fully utilised within the year and completed on schedule for the benefit of the people, state development and local communities,” it added.
The ministry said the 13MP targets zero development projects remaining not started in the second year after approval by 2030. — Bernama

Title: LCS 1, LCS 2 piping, wiring work remain behind target, A-G’s report finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Progress on piping and wiring work for Littoral Combat Ships (LCS) 1 and 2 remains behind target, putting subsequent construction activities and the targeted physical handover (PHO) of LCS 1 at risk.
According to the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026, as of June 25, piping work on LCS 1 and LCS 2 had reached only 87.70 per cent and 74.73 per cent, respectively, resulting in delays of 12.30 and 25.27 percentage points.
The delays involved 4,113 pipe spools following design changes that required rework, including pipe rerouting to meet performance targets and resolve clashes.
Meanwhile, wiring work on LCS 1 and LCS 2 had reached 51.41 per cent and 43.49 per cent, respectively, representing delays of 48.59 and 56.51 percentage points.
According to the report, the delays in wiring work are partly due to rework following design revisions involving 95 cable tray changes and 85 penetration changes.
It also said delays in piping and wiring work, which are part of the shipbuilding activities, could affect subsequent construction work and the targeted physical handover (PHO) of LCS 1.
Based on feedback from the Defence Ministry (Mindef) on July 20 and August 13, piping work for LCS 1 and LCS 2 uses a combination of pipe spools from the original and revised designs, while LCS 3 to LCS 5 use the revised design exclusively.
The delay was first identified in November 2025 following a comment from the Design Authority, Naval Group. As of July 2026, piping work on LCS 1 had reached 100 per cent, while LCS 2 stood at 96 per cent.
Mindef said the improved progress was driven by the contractor’s decision to introduce three work shifts from January 23, 2024, to accelerate completion.
However, the LCS Project Management (PPLCS) could not verify the progress of the piping and cabling work because, as of July 2026, the contractor had not submitted reports or evidence that the work had been carried out in line with the reported progress.
PPLCS will only verify work progress formally submitted by the contractor, with only work that has been physically verified and fully supported by documentation recognised as confirmed progress.
PPLCS was also informed that the actual physical progress of some activities exceeded the verified progress, but stressed that only verified and confirmed work is recorded, with unverified work excluded. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia haze worsens overnight as unhealthy areas nearly double to 21, Johor hardest hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Haze conditions worsened sharply across Malaysia overnight, with 21 areas recording unhealthy air quality as of 8am today, almost double the 11 reported yesterday afternoon.
Johor was the worst-affected state, accounting for eight of the unhealthy readings, according to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
Batu Pahat recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading nationwide at 188, followed by Kluang at 169, Segamat and Larkin at 166, Pasir Gudang at 165 and Tangkak at 164.
Kota Tinggi recorded an API of 155, while Pengerang stood at 154.
Elsewhere, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan recorded 161 and Seremban 157, while Bandaraya Melaka registered 155.
Balok Baru Kuantan in Pahang recorded an API of 153, Putrajaya 152 and Rompin, also in Pahang, 152.
Unhealthy readings were also recorded at Indera Mahkota Kuantan at 142, Cheras at 140, Kemaman at 134, Batu Muda at 120, Bukit Rambai at 115, Paka at 111 and Jerantut at 102.
The deterioration was not uniform nationwide. IPD Serian in Sarawak and Johan Setia in Selangor, which had recorded unhealthy air quality yesterday afternoon, improved to moderate readings of 98 this morning.
A further 41 areas recorded moderate air quality, while only five stations remained in the good range: Minden in Penang at 45, Kota Kinabalu at 44, Kangar at 35, Langkawi at 29 and Balik Pulau at 23.
The latest readings mark a broad worsening from 4pm yesterday, when 11 areas were classified as unhealthy and 55 as moderate.
Under Malaysia’s API scale, readings between zero and 50 are considered good, 51 to 100 moderate and 101 to 200 unhealthy. Readings of 201 to 300 are classified as very unhealthy, while anything above 300 is deemed hazardous.
Malaysia has faced recurring bouts of haze in recent weeks, with air quality deteriorating at different times across the Klang Valley, southern states and parts of Sarawak.
Earlier this month, several Klang Valley areas, including Johan Setia, Shah Alam, Nilai, Putrajaya, Klang and Cheras, recorded unhealthy readings as haze spread across the region.
Sarawak was also hit by a more severe episode in late August, when several stations recorded very unhealthy and hazardous readings, including Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman and Kuching.
The government has previously resorted to cloud-seeding operations during periods of prolonged haze, while authorities continue to monitor air quality through 68 monitoring stations nationwide.
API readings are updated hourly through APIMS.

Title: A-G’s report: RM2.55m in allowances paid without valid authority
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A total of RM2.55 million from the Light Dues Fund (KWDA) and Marine Trade Centre Fund (KWPPL) was spent on allowances and facilities in 2025 without valid authority, according to the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026.
Of the amount, RM2.31 million involved KWDA funds, while RM239,784 was from KWPPL.
According to the report, an audit of KWDA expenditure in 2025 found that RM2.31 million was paid as allowances and facilities to the KWDA Board and officers of the Malaysian Marine Department (JLM) without valid authority.
The payments were part of the total expenditure of KWDA and KWPPL, which amounted to RM131.98 million and RM6.77 million respectively in 2025.
As at December 31, 2025, KWDA had a balance of RM273.12 million, with receipts totalling RM103.48 million during the year, while KWPPL recorded a balance of RM24.72 million with receipts of RM5.81 million.
The report stated that the RM2.55 million in allowances and facilities was not provided for under the Federation Light Dues Act 1953 (Act 250), Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952 and Financial Procedure Act 1957 (Act 61).
In its response dated July 2, 2026, JLM explained that the KWDA Board and KWPPL Committee were two separate entities established under different provisions and regulations, and therefore the payment of allowances was carried out based on the rules and decisions in force for each entity.
JLM also informed that the KWDA Board had approved the Lighthouse Board Regulations 2016, which stipulated fixed allowances and facilities for the Chairman and Board members in carrying out their functions and responsibilities as provided under Act 250.
According to JLM, the Management Representative, Secretary, Chief Collector, Meeting Secretariat and Operations Officer were also entitled to allowances and facilities at the approved rates. Officers with a direct interest were not involved in the consideration process, while decisions were made collectively.
However, the Audit concluded that KWDA and KWPPL constituted public funds, the use of which was subject to the laws governing the respective funds, Act 61 and the financial regulations in force.
Accordingly, the KWDA Board and KWPPL Committee were found not to have valid authority to approve the payment of the RM2.55 million in allowances and facilities.
LKAN also stated that Act 61 stipulated that for matters not specifically provided for, approval for payments was subject to the Minister’s jurisdiction. — Bernama

Title: E-Jamin operated without formal govt contract for five years, PAC finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The e-Jamin system, used in 192 courts nationwide, has operated for five years since 2020 without a formal contract between the government and its operator, Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, due to an initial interpretation that it was merely a commercial transaction.
Public Accounts Committee (PAC) member Syahredzan Johan said the system was originally introduced as a Proof of Concept in 2017 before being expanded nationwide for bail payments, but was not followed by a proper government procurement process or a formal agreement.
He said the situation stemmed partly from a December 20, 2019 view by the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) Advisory Division, which deemed e-Jamin transactions as commercial, with courts acting only as users.
“There was an interpretation from the AGC stating that no agreement was needed between the two parties as it was just a commercial transaction,” he said when winding up the debate on the PAC Report on the Management of Court Bail Payment Services through the e-Jamin System in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Following that, he said the Finance Ministry (MOF) issued a letter of no objection to the proposal on December 26, 2019, subject to compliance with financial conditions, government data ownership, and the drafting of an agreement.
“Unfortunately, from the time the letter of no objection was issued until we conducted the investigation, no agreement was signed between the two parties,” Syahredzan said.
He said PAC found conflicting interpretations among government agencies regarding the status of bail funds before the matter was finalised through an official AGC review.
He noted that the AGC, supported by the Prime Minister’s Department and Accountant General’s Department (JANM), confirmed that bail collected under the Criminal Procedure Code constitutes public funds under Section 3 of the Financial Procedure Act 1957.
“Consequently, depositing bail funds into a private commercial bank account and failing to account for it in the Consolidated Trust Account is a clear violation of Article 97(1) of the Federal Constitution and Section 7 of Act 61,” he said.
He added that while PAC acknowledged e-Jamin’s benefits in simplifying bail payments, convenience should not override proper governance and a clear legal relationship between the government and the operator.
Syahredzan said PAC would hold follow-up discussions with the government on all matters related to the system following the tabling of the report in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Seven Members of Parliament participated in the debate, including RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong), who urged for information on Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd to be disclosed in the House.
Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) raised questions about the vendor procurement process, asking whether it was conducted through an open tender.
Earlier, PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin told a press conference that e-Jamin operated without a Letter of Appointment, Letter of Acceptance, Letter of Intent, or formal contract agreement with the government.
She revealed that of the RM193.71 million bail deposit balance as of December 31, 2024, Dapat Vista had invested RM130.8 million under the company’s name, earning RM4 million to RM5 million in interest annually.
The sitting was adjourned to 10am today. — Bernama

Title: Kedah KPDN takes RON95 samples after claims of water-mixed fuel
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 6 — The Kedah Ministry of Domestic Trade and Costs of Living (KPDN) has taken RON95 petrol samples from 11 petrol stations in several districts for analysis following recent viral claims that the fuel was mixed with water.
State KPDN director Muhammad Nizam Jamaludin said the action followed public complaints that vehicles had broken down after refuelling at the affected stations.
“KPDN enforcement teams conducted inspections at 11 petrol stations today and took fuel samples from the involved tanks or pumps for inspection and further analysis.
“At the same time, preliminary inspections using the manual dipping method and a review of the Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) system readings showed no indication of the presence of water in the inspected fuel storage tanks,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the inspections covered Petron and Caltex stations in Alor Setar, Kubang Pasu, Sungai Petani and Kulim, as well as checks of fuel supply receipts, sales records and other relevant documents.
However, Muhammad Nizam said the preliminary findings were not conclusive, adding that the samples would be sent to the Department of Chemistry for analysis while the operators would also send samples to their respective oil companies’ laboratories.
“KPDN will scrutinise the analysis results and the overall investigation findings before determining the next course of action, including taking appropriate measures if there is any violation of legal provisions,” he said.
Members of the public can channel complaints via WhatsApp at 019-848 8000, the KPDN e-Aduan portal, the KPDN Call Centre at 1-800-886-800 or the KPDN EzADU smartphone application. — Bernama

Title: Perikatan’s bid to challenge ROS suspension order to be heard by High Court on Oct 13
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The High Court here yesterday set October 13 to hear Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application for leave to commence a judicial review against the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) suspension order on the coalition’s activities.
A check on the court system showed that the application will be heard before Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad at 9am.
PN and PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, along with secretaries-general of Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan) Wong Chia Zhen and Malaysian Indian People’s Party (MIPP) N. Sathes Kumar, filed the application as the first to third applicants. The fourth and fifth applicants were the secretaries-general of Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah, and Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang), Datuk Sazmi Miah.
The respondents are RoS director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
In a certificate of urgency filed through Messrs Siddiq Azani & Co alongside the application, the applicants said the suspension prevented them from conducting routine political activities. This included using the coalition’s name and symbol in the 16th Melaka State Election.
Takiyuddin, in a supporting affidavit obtained by the media, said the suspension order issued by the RoS on September 23 had a conclusive effect, as it prohibited the coalition from carrying out political activities.
He said the suspension prevented the PN Supreme Council and other party organs from convening meetings or making decisions, including those related to PN’s participation in the Melaka State Election. As a result, PN could not issue statements, hold public rallies, or campaign, adding that party officials also risked prosecution if they breached the order.
In the application, PN seeks an order of certiorari to quash the suspension order dated September 23 under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. The order suspended all PN activities except responding to a notice of intention to cancel registration.
They are also challenging a notice dated September 22, 2026, under subsection 13(2) of the same Act expressing the intention to deregister PN after 30 days.
According to the application, the notice was issued on the grounds that PN had breached Clause 7.1 of the PN Constitution by failing to invite Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), as a member party, to the PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16.
The applicants contended that the RoS lacks jurisdiction to determine whether Bersatu remains a member party of PN. They said the PN Constitution should decide this.
They also said the suspension order was made without giving PN the right to be heard. They added they were not provided with Bersatu’s complaint or the documents forming the basis of the action. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Issues on Myanmar nationals, school student safety among matters to be raised
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The presence of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia and student safety in schools are expected to be among the issues raised at today’s Dewan Rakyat sitting.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, during the Minister’s Question Time, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask the Prime Minister to outline the government’s steps to address the long-standing presence of Myanmar nationals, including refugees and asylum seekers, which has raised public concern.
Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) will ask the Prime Minister why incidents threatening student safety continue in schools despite government safety guidelines and procedures being in place.
During the Question and Answer session, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) will ask the Home Minister for the latest status on implementing 17 recommendations to strengthen security controls, screening, and risk management at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and other international gateways in the country.
The cross-border haze issue is also among the matters likely to be raised in the lower house of Parliament, with Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab (GPS-Tanjong Manis) scheduled to ask the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister about steps taken to address the problem, particularly in Sarawak.
He will also seek information on diplomatic or legal actions the ministry has taken to address the ongoing haze issue.
Following the Question and Answer session, the sitting will proceed with the first reading of the Supply Bill 2027 by the Finance Minister and the second reading of the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the Youth and Sports Minister.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament for the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to sit for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: Zetrix AI submits settlement proposal after JPJ services suspended over RM314m arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Zetrix AI Berhad has submitted a proposal to the Malaysian government to address outstanding remittances after authorities suspended its Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection services over RM314 million in unpaid government revenue.
The technology company said in a statement yesterday that resolving the outstanding obligations was its immediate priority, while efforts to restore the affected services would be subject to the relevant approvals.
“Zetrix AI has submitted a proposed solution to the Government of Malaysia to address the outstanding remittances for their consideration,” it said.
“The Group’s immediate priority is to resolve these obligations and work towards restoring the affected services, subject to the relevant approvals.”
The company did not disclose details of the proposed solution.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said yesterday that My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI, both under the MYEG Group, had failed to remit RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and September 30.
He said the authorities had issued 35 reminders and engaged the companies since May in an attempt to recover the outstanding funds before their services as government revenue collection agents were suspended.
Loke said MYEG had also issued a cheque for RM231 million dated September 30, but the payment could not be processed by the bank following instructions from the company.
“Therefore, the Ministry of Transport and the Road Transport Department had to take the drastic step of suspending payment services through MyEG and Zetrix AI from today,” he said at a press conference yesterday.
The ministry and JPJ will also initiate legal action to recover the full RM314 million, Loke said.
Zetrix AI, meanwhile, expressed regret over the inconvenience caused by the suspension, which took effect on October 5.
“As a provider of JPJ services since 2000, we understand the importance of ensuring these essential services remain accessible, reliable and convenient for the public,” it said.
“The Group recognises its responsibility to customers and remains committed to fulfilling its obligations to the Government.”
The company also assured customers who had used the affected JPJ services before the suspension that their transactions had already been processed and fulfilled.
Loke said the suspension would not disrupt JPJ services more broadly, with transactions still available through alternatives including the MyJPJ app, JPJ Public Portal, counters and kiosks.
JPJ had announced on October 2 that services provided by MyEG and Zetrix AI as collection agents would be suspended from 12.01am on October 5 following non-compliance with the terms of their agreements.
Zetrix AI, formerly known as MY E.G. Services Berhad, began operations in 2000 as a provider of electronic government services and has since expanded into blockchain and artificial intelligence services.

Title: Budget 2027: What RM425m for plantations and commodities means for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A bottle of cooking oil, a set of car tyres and a pair of rubber gloves may appear to have little in common.
Yet each begins, in one way or another, with commodities produced by the country’s plantation sector.
Those commodities do not stop at the plantation, as they are processed into products used by consumers and businesses, while also contributing to the country’s exports.
So what does the plantation and commodities sector actually cover, and why has the government proposed RM425.65 million for the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities under Budget 2027?
How will Malaysians “feel” the impact of this allocation?
Let’s take a look at what the ministry covers, where its commodities end up and how they make their way from plantations and smallholdings to consumers and export markets.
The plantation and commodities sector
The ministry oversees commodities including palm oil, rubber, cocoa, pepper, timber, kenaf, sago and tobacco, as well as related downstream activities.
These commodities move through a wider supply chain, from plantations and smallholdings to processing and manufacturing before reaching consumers or overseas markets.
Smallholders, or
pekebun kecil
, are individual farmers or families who cultivate relatively small areas of land rather than operating large commercial plantations.
They are an important part of the commodity supply chain, particularly in oil palm and rubber.
Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Noraini Ahmad has said empowering smallholders through quality inputs, good agricultural practices and support for replanting programmes is one of the ministry’s priorities to improve productivity and income.
Where does it show up in everyday life?
Cooking oil and food
Palm oil is perhaps the most familiar example.
Harvested oil palm fruit is used to make cooking oil and can also be found in a range of everyday products, including margarine, biscuits, bread, chocolate, instant noodles and other processed foods.
In the bathroom, palm-derived ingredients are also used in products such as soap, shampoo and cosmetics.
In 2024, oil palm contributed RM38.1 billion, or 36.8 per cent, of Malaysia’s agricultural value added, making it the largest contributor within the agriculture sector.
Oil palm also extends to markets abroad.
According to the Malaysian Palm Oil Board, palm oil and palm-based products generated RM112.64 billion in exports in 2025.
Tyres, gloves and rubber products
Rubber is another direct link between plantations, industry and consumers’ everyday lives.
Natural rubber and rubber-based materials are used in products such as medical gloves, tyres, rubber hoses, seals, belts and footwear.
There is also a connection between smallholders and manufacturers producing these products, as well as the healthcare, automotive and manufacturing sectors that use them.
These products are also exported, making rubber important not only as a farm commodity but also as an industrial raw material.
Apart from palm oil and rubber, cocoa, pepper, timber, kenaf and sago are other familiar commodities that appear in households or businesses.
What does the RM425m cover?
The proposed amount under Budget 2027 covers four initiatives under the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities.
Its focus is on oil palm smallholder replanting, farm roads, disaster and disease control and support for downstream agro-commodity entrepreneurs.
The largest allocation is RM280.03 million for the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0, followed by RM100 million for the Smallholder Farm Road Programme.
Another RM28.57 million is proposed for the Agro-Commodity Sector Disaster and Disease Control Fund, while RM17.05 million is proposed for downstream agro-commodity entrepreneurs.
The four areas address different needs — maintaining future production, improving access to farms, protecting crops and supporting businesses.
Why is replanting important?
Oil palm trees become less productive as they age, so replacing older trees can help maintain production, but newly planted trees take time before they start producing at useful levels.
For smallholders, replanting can also mean taking on the cost of clearing and planting again while waiting for the new trees to mature.
It also matters to the wider sector because maintaining oil palm production helps ensure there is enough supply for domestic processing and Malaysia’s export market.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the replanting programme would continue to help improve the productivity and income of smallholders in the long term.
Farm roads are crucial too
A farm road may seem like a very specific issue for people who do not live or work in plantations, but it can affect how produce is harvested and how equipment moves between farms, collection centres and mills.
A simple way to look at it is:
Oil palm fruit → collection → mill → processing → manufacturing → consumer or export market
Anwar, in his latest remarks, said the proposed farm road projects should provide basic infrastructure suited to plantation areas and directly improve smallholders’ productivity.
Does the price of commodities directly affect what we pay?
A change in the global price of palm oil or rubber does not automatically mean the price of a product on a supermarket shelf will change by the same amount.
Other costs are involved, including processing, packaging, transport, labour, exchange rates and business margins.
Government controls or subsidies can also affect the final price of some products.
For example, a rise in palm oil prices could increase costs for businesses that use palm-based inputs.
However, how much that affects the final price depends on the product and the other costs involved.
The same applies to rubber.
For example, a change in rubber prices can affect manufacturers, but it does not mean the price of a new set of tyres will immediately change by the same amount.
How do exports impact us?
The sector is not just about products used in Malaysia.
Malaysia also exports commodities and commodity-based products, bringing in foreign earnings and supporting businesses involved in processing, manufacturing, logistics and trade.
The commodity sector and commodity-based industries contributed RM19.65 billion to Malaysia’s GDP in the first quarter of 2026, while exports of commodity-based products generated RM41.62 billion during the same period, according to Noraini.
This is why what happens after commodities leave the farm also matters.
When more processing and manufacturing takes place in Malaysia, more economic activity can be generated locally before a product is sold here or exported.
What happens when production falls?
This is where replanting, disease control and measures to address climate-related disruptions are crucial.
If production of an important commodity falls, there may be less raw material for Malaysian processors and manufacturers.
Businesses could then face higher costs or have to look elsewhere for supplies, depending on market conditions.
For Malaysia, lower production can also affect the amount of commodities available for export and the earnings generated from them.
This is why some of the Budget 2027 allocation is focused on maintaining production and protecting crops, rather than only helping with immediate consumer needs.
So, how will Malaysians feel the impact?
The RM425.65 million proposed under Budget 2027 is not a direct payment to consumers.
For Malaysians, the impact could be seen through more productive smallholders, better movement of agricultural produce, stronger domestic processing and more resilient supply chains.
There is also a wider economic benefit if Malaysian companies can continue producing and exporting commodity-based products competitively.
So while the allocation may start with plantations and smallholdings, its effects can extend much further — to the products Malaysians use, the businesses that depend on these commodities and the exports that contribute to the economy.

Title: IGP: Police record statements from 25 witnesses in KLIA incident involving border agency chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Police have recorded statements from 25 witnesses as part of investigations into allegations that the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) physically assaulted two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28.
In a statement issued today, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said that the two officers had lodged police reports over the alleged incident.
The case is being investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department at Bukit Aman under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which covers voluntarily causing hurt.
Those convicted under the provision face up to one year in prison, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
The 25 witnesses whose statements have been recorded include PDRM officers and personnel, AKPS officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary police personnel, baggage-handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses.
PDRM said the investigation was being conducted transparently, professionally and impartially, based on witness statements and evidence gathered to ensure all aspects of the incident were examined thoroughly.
The investigation papers will be referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on October 6 for consideration, advice and further directions, in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.
The public has also been advised against making speculation or drawing conclusions that could affect the ongoing investigation and legal process.

Title: Higher education minister: Universities not only path to youth success
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The public need to change the perception that universities are the only avenue for developing talent and determining the success of young people, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said knowledge and skills in technical fields also opened up career opportunities for young people, including those who were less academically inclined.
"Over the past two years, we have often told the people that universities are not the only place for them to pursue their studies, but we also have other skills institutions such as polytechnics and community colleges that offer skills certificates in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
"For years, society has viewed polytechnics as a second choice for those who cannot get into university, but now applications to enter polytechnics have reached 132 per cent compared with 60 to 70 per cent previously,” he said.
He said this during the "Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?” dialogue session held in conjunction with the launch of the Future Skills Framework for the Communications Sector and the Strategic Talent Development Initiative at Angkasapuri today.
Zambry said teaching approaches at skills institutions were also being strengthened to meet the country’s demand for technical workers, including the government’s effort to produce 60,000 engineers.
He said technical and engineering fields did not necessarily depend solely on degree qualifications, but also required skilled workers who had undergone engineering-related training at skills institutions.
Students from the arts stream with an interest and potential in the field were also being given opportunities to pursue it through suitable intervention programmes, he said, adding that polytechnics had so far trained 447 students through engineering diploma programmes.
Meanwhile, Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the skills mismatch issue needed attention, with nearly 37 per cent of skilled workers recorded as not working in the second quarter of this year, while the country’s workforce stood at 16.8 million.
He said the situation was attributed, among other factors, to a lack of job opportunities, skills mismatches and less attractive salary offers in certain fields, making it necessary to strengthen the "future-proof talent” approach to ensure workers’ skills were aligned earlier with future job requirements.
In efforts to strengthen workforce development, he said the Ministry of Human Resources had introduced the National Human Resources Policy 2026-2035, focusing on four aspects - more productive employment, career development, more meaningful incomes and appropriate protection.
However, Khairul Firdaus said the effectiveness of the policy needed to be supported by more balanced infrastructure development between states to ensure job opportunities and talent development were not concentrated only in the Klang Valley. — Bernama

Title: Defence minister: LCS missile compensation claim expected to take time
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Recovering funds linked to the procurement of missiles for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will not be resolved immediately and will take time, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said the delay is due to a lack of cooperation from the Norwegian government in resolving the issue.
He said that although requests for Norway’s assistance had been made at various levels, including by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), Foreign Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan) and himself, Norway had refused to intervene.
“We do not see this matter being resolved quickly… even though Norway is the cause of the problem by refusing to grant the export licence.
“It (Norway) has done nothing to help us reach a decision that safeguards our rights and interests,” he said after the launch of the Siber Siaga 2026, held in conjunction with the Cyber Digital Services, Defence & Security Asia (CyberDSA) 2026 exhibition at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.
Mohamed Khaled said the Norwegian government’s lack of intervention has left Malaysia to pursue its claim directly with the company, which he said has given various excuses.
“Recovering our money will not be easy. We expect it to be a lengthy process,” he said, stressing that efforts to complete the LCS weapon systems must continue regardless of the outcome of the claim against the supplier.
He said he would raise the matter with the government to discuss funding for new missiles, with the procurement involving several complex considerations, including the delivery timeframe.
The ministry must also ensure the new missiles can integrate with the LCS’s Combat Management System (CMS), which is nearing completion.
Malaysia reportedly has taken legal action against missile supplier Kongsberg Defense & Aerospace AS to seek compensation after the Norwegian government canceled the export license for Naval Strike Missiles (NSM) intended for the LCS project. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
He said cooperation between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and schools should be strengthened to ensure all incidents are reported for further action.
“Sometimes there are actions by certain parties attempting to hide issues to protect their reputation. But I believe if we enhance and strengthen this relationship, it can help resolve the problems,” he told a press conference after the launch of the PDRM Negotiator Handbook at the Bukit Aman Senior Officers' Mess here today.
Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.
He added that PDRM holds regular discussions with schools and parent-teacher associations on safety measures, including proposals to install closed-circuit television (CCTV). The Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) has also increased patrols at schools and hostels.
On the death of a 16-year-old student at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, he said some details remain unconfirmed and the department will conduct a thorough investigation before making any conclusions.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid said PDRM has strengthened its Negotiator Cell, which was set up two years ago, by introducing a handbook for officers to use during crisis negotiations.
He said the cell, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA), has about 40 officers from various departments. The officers are selected based on their experience and can be deployed if a crisis requires negotiation expertise.
"If a crisis such as a kidnapping occurs, requiring advice, views, or negotiation between relevant parties, we will call upon the officers concerned to carry out the negotiation," he said.
He said the Negotiator Cell also works with other PDRM divisions as needed. The unit has also given lectures and shared experience in crisis management with the Royal Brunei Police Force.
Bukit Aman KDNKA deputy director (Crisis and Disaster) and Negotiator Cell commandant Datuk M.V Srikumar Nair said no standard response time is set for each case, as the duration depends on the circumstances and uniqueness of an incident.
"Every case is unique. Some information is received quickly, while other cases take time. Therefore, there is no standard response time," he said. — Bernama

Title: Johor MB: State government ready to help schools review security measures following student’s death
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The Johor state government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
He said this is to prevent a recurrence of the incident that led to the death of 16-year-old Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a secondary school in Yong Peng, near here.
Onn Hafiz expressed full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry (MOE), particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within school premises.
"We have received a report on the incident and will look into every angle and opportunity to ensure student safety is better guaranteed," he said, adding that he would liaise with the ministry regarding student safety issues.
Speaking to reporters after visiting the victim's family in Kampung Parit Selamat today, he expressed deep sorrow on behalf of the state government, while urging the public to give police space to conduct a thorough investigation and refrain from speculation.
Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD).
He said the meeting would re-examine safety standard operating procedures (SOPs) in detail to address any existing weaknesses or shortcomings.
"This is not a matter to be taken lightly as it involves the loss of a life," he said.
On Saturday (Oct 3), Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and bleeding in the school hall at about 5.50 pm.
Johor Police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the victim sustained injuries to her head and body and was pronounced dead at the scene.
Police subsequently detained a 16-year-old boy in Yong Peng at about 7 pm the same day. He was later remanded in custody for six days until Oct 9 to assist in investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Land encroachment must be taken seriously
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Good governance practices must continue to be upheld, while any form of unauthorised land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said enforcement must therefore continue to be strengthened, while any related issues raised by stakeholders, including non-governmental organisations (NGOs), should be addressed promptly to ensure accurate and transparent information is communicated comprehensively and effectively.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he stressed these points while chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting.
“As we confront the effects of climate change, land governance can no longer focus solely on economic returns or physical development.
“Land management must be carried out prudently and systematically to minimise risks to environmental sustainability,” he said.
Anwar said the Madani Government would continue to ensure that land management initiatives were carried out responsibly for the benefit of the people. — Bernama

Title: Warehouse worker pleads not guilty to driving under the influence, injuring two marathon runners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 —An e-commerce platform warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol, causing injuries to two participants of a running event last Saturday.
Muhammad Saiful Sabinee, 21, was charged with riding a motorcycle against the flow of traffic with an alcohol level of 184 milligrams (mg) per 100 millilitres (ml) of blood, resulting in injuries to Mazni Lamin, 50, and Azwan Ibrahim, 41, on Jalan Munshi, near a clothing store here, at 6.14 am on Oct 3.
The charges were framed under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a minimum prison sentence of seven years and a maximum of 10 years, as well as a fine of up to RM50,000, upon conviction.
The provision also stipulates that a person convicted may be disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence for a period of not less than seven years from the date of conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurbatrisyia Mohd Razib proposed bail of RM10,000 with one surety for each charge, noting that the accused did not possess a driving licence.
Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation, representing Muhammad Saiful, appealed for a bail reduction, saying that his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month.
“My client has four siblings, one of whom is still in school, and his mother is present today to act as his surety,” he said.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar granted Muhammad Saiful bail of RM500 with one surety for each charge and set Jan 7, 2027, for case mention and submission of documents. — Bernama

Title: Govt launches framework to prepare communications, multimedia workforce for AI-driven changes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The federal government today launched a new framework to align communications and multimedia industry needs with education and skills development as artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, emerging technologies and the green economy reshape the sector.
Led by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the Communications and Multimedia Future Skills Framework (C&M FSF) will serve as a strategic reference for talent development in the communications and multimedia sector over the next five to 10 years.
Its implementation will also involve the Higher Education and Human Resources ministries to align industry needs with education and skills development.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the framework identifies industry needs while aligning government, industry and education efforts to keep talent development in step with technological and economic changes.
“AI is already changing the nature of many jobs, particularly in areas such as advertising, graphic design and production, by speeding up work processes and taking over some tasks.
“So it is a guideline that we will study and apply across specific sectors under MCMC’s purview, particularly broadcasting, telecommunications and postal and courier services,” he told reporters after the launch of the framework at Angkasapuri here.
Fahmi said the framework was not regulatory in nature, but focused on workforce needs and the potential impact of AI adoption on the sectors and their long-term planning.
To ensure the C&M FSF meets industry needs, the Future Skills Talent Council (FSTC) has been established under the Human Resources Ministry in collaboration with the Communications Ministry through MCMC.
Meanwhile, the Higher Education Ministry will use the C&M FSF to strengthen curricula, micro-credentials and graduate competencies, while training and upskilling programmes will be tailored to changing technology and job market needs.
Fahmi said the framework’s launch reflected the federal government’s efforts to anticipate changes in the job landscape and prepare Malaysians with future-ready skills.
“On the government’s part, we will work to ensure there are more job opportunities available, enabling companies to hire more people, especially young Malaysians,” he said.

Title: ‘Touch ‘n Go rep’ scam leaves Kedah woman RM150 poorer, says consumer group
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 5 — A 39-year-old self-employed woman lost about RM150, including her BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) petrol subsidy and reward points, after a phone scammer posing as a Touch ‘n Go representative compromised her e-wallet.
Kedah Consumers Association (Cake) president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said the victim lodged a report at the association’s office yesterday.
“The victim said the caller offered her a new Touch ‘n Go card with various perks, including reward points, store vouchers offering discounts of up to 80 per cent, and overseas spending capabilities.
“After she agreed to apply for the card, the caller instructed her to open her Touch ‘n Go e-wallet application and follow specific instructions,” he said in a statement today.
He added that without her knowledge, the fraudster took over the application and accessed her account.
“Cake has advised her to report the matter to both the police and Touch ‘n Go.
“Several other individuals have since come forward stating they were also targeted. Cake advises the public to exercise caution regarding unsolicited telephone offers, as fraudsters are resorting to various tricks to deceive people,” he said. — Bernama
